messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: PD-11004 fired for route /v1/chat/generate — p99 > 2s sustained for 2 mins. Alert rule: latency-tail-uswest.
frank_oncall: Acking PD-11004. I'm joining the bridge. Starting with recent config changes and autoscaler state.
pagerduty-bot: PD-11004 acknowledged by frank_oncall. Escalation paused.
geeta_sre: I see the spike in us-west. p95 jumped from 180ms -> 520ms, p99 ~ 2100ms. Inflight token queues increased, but CPU/GPU util looks okay.
hannah_eng: Any recent infra or model ops pushes?
config-bot: Deploy: config-service:feature-flags rolled at 4851236600 by ops-bot — changes: enable: cache_bypass_experiment=true for route /v1/chat/generate (targeted).
frank_oncall: That stands out. Can someone check whether requests are bypassing prefix/KV cache?
geeta_sre: Checking cache logs... kv-cache logs show a flood of 'miss' and 'bypass=true' for that route starting at 4851236612. Hit rate dropped 90% -> 12%.
hannah_eng: WTF. The feature flag was supposed to be gated for internal canary users only. Looks like rollout targeted prod by mistake. Rolling it back now.
config-bot: Rolling back feature flag cache_bypass_experiment -> false (started by hannah_eng).
incident-bot: Action recorded: feature flag rollback started at 4851236720.
ivan_support: We have 3 customers reporting slow responses and one timed-out webhook (ORG-712). CS is on it.
geeta_sre: Observability snapshot:
```
route: /v1/chat/generate
p50: 140ms
p95: 520ms (+340ms)
p99: 2100ms (+1.9s)
kv_cache_hit: 12% (was 94% before 4851236610)
inflight: 640
batch_avg: 7.1
errors: 0.1%
```
frank_oncall: Reverting flag should help but we need immediate relief while caches repopulate. Options: route-split to warm pool in us-east, reduce batch size at edge for this route, or temporary short-circuit to smaller model for 25% traffic. Which is fastest?
geeta_sre: Reducing batch_size_max at edge is fastest (no rollout), will reduce p99 tail. Initiating config change to max_batch_size=4 for route. Also pre-warming caches by replaying recent hot prefixes on a warm pool.
hannah_eng: Starting small-model fallback for 20% now. Also kicking off cache warm job for top-10 prefixes.
incident-bot: Actions: edge config max_batch_size=4 applied by geeta_sre. route-split: 80/20 to model-small started by hannah_eng. Cache-warm job queued.
pagerduty-bot: PD-11004 note: mitigation steps applied.
ivan_support: CS update draft: "We've identified a misrouted feature flag that caused cache bypass for some production requests, leading to increased latency. Mitigations are in progress and we observe partial recovery." Approving to send.
frank_oncall: Send the update. Keep PD open until p99 < 600ms for 20m.
incident-bot: Timeline note: feature flag rolled at 4851236600, spike detected 4851236689, rollback started 4851236720, mitigation configs applied 4851236775.
geeta_sre: After batch cap and 80/20 split, measurable improvement: p99 down to ~850ms, kv_hit climbing to 48% (3m after rollback).
hannah_eng: Cache warm job running; warm hits increasing. Also found the root cause: the flag's targeting rule used an incorrect regex that matched all org IDs when empty audience list and fallback were misinterpreted by config-service. Fixing targeting logic in config-service and adding stricter validation.
frank_oncall: Good find. Is there any sign of secondary issues (evictions/ooms) from the bypass surge?
geeta_sre: A couple of cache-worker pods reported elevated GC pauses and one restarted once during the surge window but restarted healthy. No persistent OOMs.
ivan_support: Customer impact: ORG-712 saw 5 user-facing slow calls and one webhook timeout; ORG-204 reported slowness but no failures. CS sent initial notice.
frank_oncall: Once p99 < 600ms and stable for 20m we'll resolve. Current p99 ~420ms, p95 ~260ms, kv_hit 82%.
incident-bot: PD-11004 update posted by ivan_support.
pagerduty-bot: PD-11004 status: acknowledged; awaiting resolution criteria.
hannah_eng: Post-incident actions I propose: (1) add validation to config-service to reject empty audience + fallback that expands to all; (2) add canary gating + manual approval for feature-flag changes that touch production routes; (3) add SLO on kv_cache_hit for critical routes.
geeta_sre: I'll own SLO alert PR (infra-alerts). I'll also add a dashboard showing feature-flag rollout vs cache hit for correlation.
ivan_support: I'll collate customer impact and timestamps for postmortem.
frank_oncall: Handoff: I will keep incident open and hand to emma_oncall at 4851239000 for postmortem authoring. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PD-11004 will remain open for postmortem and assigned next oncall emma_oncall.
